summary: A temporary manual process replaces automated wire exception repair for six months. The key drivers are operator ability to edit beneficiary details before release, single-operator handling below CAD 50,000, cross-border corridors including Mexico, and tracking in a shared spreadsheet. No new customers, channels or third parties are introduced.

dimensions.narrative: No product change; existing wire product.
Existing retail and commercial wire senders.
Existing corridors include Mexico, a higher-risk jurisdiction.
Repaired wires up to CAD 250,000 re-enter monitoring; beneficiary edits could bypass original screening context.
Shared spreadsheet tracking is a weak control environment.
Manual beneficiary edits with single-operator release below CAD 50,000 is the main exposure.

claims.text: A material process change may not go live without a completed financial crime risk assessment approved by the Risk Committee.

citations.quote: without a completed financial crime risk assessment reviewed by an FCRM analyst and approved by the Risk Committee

claims.text: Cross-border activity to Mexico requires enhanced monitoring.

citations.quote: Mexico and Brazil are designated higher-risk jurisdictions for cross-border payment products

claims.text: Manually repaired cross-border wires to higher-risk jurisdictions still require real-time monitoring.

citations.quote: Cross-border payments require real-time monitoring for cross-border activity to higher-risk jurisdictions
